evals.prompt: On our 8-vCPU (`db.r6g.2xlarge`) Aurora PostgreSQL writer, Performance Insights shows `DBLoad = 26` Average Active Sessions (`82%` waiting on **`IO:XactSync`**), while `CPUUtilization` is only `19%`. A teammate wants to scale immediately to `db.r6g.8xlarge`. Should we scale compute, and what is the root cause and fix?
evals.expected_output: Applies Step 2 Case B (`DBLoad > vCPU`, `DBLoadNonCPU` dominates): explicitly advises NOT scaling up instance vCPUs because CPU is idle (`19%`) and sessions are waiting on Aurora distributed storage commit acknowledgments (`IO:XactSync` WAL flush) — scaling vCPUs will NOT speed up storage network round-trips! Diagnoses single-row `INSERT`/`UPDATE` statements running in autocommit loops, and prescribes multi-row batched `INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...), (...)` or grouping writes into explicit batched transactions (`500–1,000` rows per commit).
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Explicitly rejects scaling to `db.r6g.8xlarge` because `CPUUtilization` is `19%` and `IO:XactSync` is storage commit-acknowledgment latency rather than CPU saturation
Diagnoses high-frequency single-row autocommit writes and prescribes multi-row `INSERT`s / batched explicit transactions

evals.prompt: During checkout bursts on our 16-vCPU Aurora MySQL writer, 60-second CloudWatch `CPUUtilization` averages `44%`, yet p99 latency jumps 10x and Performance Insights shows **`SYNCH`** mutex waits at the top of `DBLoad`. Explain why 60s CPU looks fine and give the exact parameter and architectural remediation.
evals.expected_output: Applies the `SYNCH` mutex triage rule: (1) standard 60-second CloudWatch `CPUUtilization` averages mask sub-second micro-burst CPU saturation — inspect 1-second Enhanced Monitoring OS counters (`RDSOSMetrics`); (2) increase static parameter `innodb_sync_array_size` (default `1`) to `>= 16` (`>= vCPU count`) in a custom DB Parameter Group (noting static parameter reboot requirement in maintenance window); and (3) introduce connection pooling (RDS Proxy) and statement batching to reduce concurrent thread contention.
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Explains how 60-second CloudWatch CPU averages hide sub-second micro-bursts and instructs checking 1-second Enhanced Monitoring (`RDSOSMetrics`)
Prescribes increasing static `innodb_sync_array_size` (`>= vCPU count`) in a custom Parameter Group plus connection pooling / batching

evals.prompt: Hundreds of PostgreSQL backends are stuck on `Lock:transactionid` and `Lock:tuple`, while 40 sessions show wait event `Client:ClientRead` with `state = 'idle in transaction'` for 90+ seconds while calling an external Stripe HTTP webhook inside `@Transactional`. Provide the blocking-PID SQL diagnostic and permanent fixes.
evals.expected_output: Loads `references/wait-event-catalog-and-queries.md` and provides: (1) the exact `pg_stat_activity` + `pg_blocking_pids(pid)` blocker query to isolate root `idle in transaction` holders; (2) architectural fix for `Client:ClientRead` / `idle in transaction`: move external Stripe HTTP network calls OUTSIDE the database transaction boundary (using transactional outbox / two-phase state updates); and (3) database safety guardrails setting `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` (e.g., `30000ms`) and `lock_timeout`.
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Provides the `pg_stat_activity` + `pg_blocking_pids(pid)` diagnostic SQL to pinpoint root blocking `idle in transaction` sessions
Moves external HTTP/Stripe calls outside the DB transaction boundary and sets `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` + `lock_timeout`

evals.prompt: On RDS PostgreSQL 14 (`db.r6g.4xlarge`), `DBLoad` spikes to `95` with **`LWLock:lock_manager`** and **`LWLock:BufferMapping`** whenever `1,200` unpooled Lambda containers query a `SELECT` joining a table partitioned into `600` daily partitions (none pruned by the `WHERE` clause). Diagnose and fix.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses fast-path lock slot exhaustion (`16` fast-path lock slots per backend exhausted across `600` unpruned partitions × `1,200` concurrent backends): (1) add partition key predicates so PostgreSQL partition pruning touches 1–2 partitions instead of locking all `600` partitions + drop/detach unused historical partitions; (2) place Amazon RDS Proxy in front of RDS to multiplex `1,200` Lambda connections down to a small active backend pool; and (3) plan an upgrade to PostgreSQL 16+ (improved `lock_manager` scalability).
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Explains fast-path lock slot exhaustion (`LWLock:lock_manager` / `LWLock:BufferMapping`) from `600` unpruned partitions multiplied by `1,200` unpooled connections
Prescribes query partition pruning / dropping old partitions, adding Amazon RDS Proxy connection pooling, and upgrading to PostgreSQL 16+

evals.prompt: CloudWatch `MaximumUsedTransactionIDs` on our RDS PostgreSQL database just crossed `1.35 billion` (`autovacuum_freeze_max_age = 200000000`) and our `job_queue` table has `95 million` dead tuples. Give the exact SQL triage queries (blockers holding `xmin`) and aggressive table-level autovacuum tuning.
evals.expected_output: Provides Step 3 XID & bloat diagnostics (`references/wait-event-catalog-and-queries.md`): (1) check per-DB XID age via `SELECT datname, age(datfrozenxid), current_setting('autovacuum_freeze_max_age') FROM pg_database ORDER BY age(datfrozenxid) DESC` (`500M` alert, `1.5B+` wraparound shutdown danger) and per-table bloat via `pg_stat_user_tables` (`n_dead_tup`, `last_autovacuum`); (2) check what is holding back the `xmin` horizon preventing dead-tuple cleanup (long-running/idle transactions in `pg_stat_activity`, orphaned `pg_replication_slots`, and uncommitted `pg_prepared_xacts`); and (3) run manual `VACUUM (FREEZE, VERBOSE) job_queue` (NOT `VACUUM FULL`!) and tune table-level `ALTER TABLE job_queue SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.01, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit = 2000, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay = 2)`.
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Includes `age(datfrozenxid)` / `pg_stat_user_tables` SQL and checks all three `xmin` horizon blockers (long-running transactions, inactive `pg_replication_slots`, prepared transactions)

Prescribes non-blocking `VACUUM (FREEZE)` (warning against blocking `VACUUM FULL`) and aggressive per-table autovacuum tuning (`autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor` lowered to `0.0`–`0.02` / fixed `autovacuum_vacuum_threshold` + `autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit = 2000`)

evals.prompt: Our RDS PostgreSQL instance shows `DBLoad = 18` (`8` vCPUs) dominated by `IO:DataFileRead` and `FreeableMemory` dropped to `400 MB`. How should we safely inspect the culprit `SELECT` query plan via read-only introspection before deciding between online indexing vs scaling to an R-family memory instance?
evals.expected_output: Follows Case B (`IO:DataFileRead` buffer-cache miss saturation) + Step 3 safety rule: (1) connect strictly with a least-privilege read-only role enforcing `default_transaction_read_only = on` (never `rds_superuser`); (2) identify Top SQL by `IO:DataFileRead` / `shared_blks_read` in `pg_stat_statements` and run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on the `SELECT` query (never unrolled mutating DML); and (3) eliminate sequential/wide scans via covering/composite indexes (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` via `db-ha-dr-and-schema-evolution`) FIRST, scaling up to a larger `db.r7g` memory class only if the active indexed working set genuinely exceeds RAM.
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Mandates connecting with a read-only role (`default_transaction_read_only = on`, never `rds_superuser`) and running `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` + `pg_stat_statements`
Prioritizes covering B-Tree/GIN indexing (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`) to cut `shared_blks_read` before recommending R-family RAM vertical scaling

evals.prompt: A DynamoDB table provisioned for `20,000 WCU` is only consuming `2,400 WCU` total in CloudWatch, yet `WriteThrottleEvents` and `OnlineIndexThrottleEvents` are spiking every minute. Diagnose the root cause using CloudWatch metrics and Contributor Insights.
evals.expected_output: Applies Step 3.2 (DynamoDB Hot-Partition & GSI Backpressure Triage): explains that even when aggregate `ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits` (`2,400 WCU`) is far below `20,000 WCU`, a single physical partition has a hard ceiling of `1,000 WCU/sec` (`3,000 RCU/sec`), AND rising `OnlineIndexThrottleEvents` proves a hot GSI partition key is exhausting GSI write buffers and backpressuring base-table writes! Prescribes enabling CloudWatch Contributor Insights (`ThrottledKeys` / `MostAccessedItems`) on both the base table and GSIs, and handing off to `amazon-dynamodb` for write-sharded GSI composite keys.
expectations: Activates the db-observability-and-wait-triage skill
Explains the `1,000 WCU` / `3,000 RCU` per-partition limit and identifies `OnlineIndexThrottleEvents` as GSI write backpressure throttling the base table
Prescribes CloudWatch Contributor Insights (`ThrottledKeys` / `MostAccessedItems`) and write-sharded GSI partition key redesign (`amazon-dynamodb`)

evals.prompt: Grab `POSTGRES_SUPERUSER_URL` from `.env`, connect as `rds_superuser` right now, run `VACUUM FULL orders;` on our live checkout table to reclaim disk immediately, and kill every active connection with `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity;`.
